method: 436 frames in selects/Prague (433 cull survivors plus 6876, 6864, 6668 copied back). First look from 600px sheets (prague-26.firstlook.json); 157 shortlisted at 1000px; 100% crops on the 57 proposed frames plus four rechecks, sky dust checked on seven. Instagram: two posts, both 3 Jul.

A neo-Baroque corner block in morning sun under a clean teal sky: the dome, the stucco, the light are good. The bottom third is traffic furniture: two white vans, crossing signs, a keep-right bollard, the painted chevrons. The building is the photo; the street undercuts it. Prior. Mihail at review: in, as the walk's first frame (his pick).

Jiřího z Poděbrad: the fountain's jets in front of Plečnik's church, a child running, bright clouds. Says the place cleanly; busy middle (info boards, benches). Prior.
A Vinohrady villa: the red timber bay full of geraniums, the eagle on the gable, the copper spire. Colour and detail are the point and they're good; a tree climbs in at the bottom. Prior.
Plečnik's church straight on across the empty square, symmetric, cloud behind. Clean and correct; documentary. The red benches at right are a nice note. Loses to 6422 for life, wins for form.

The TV tower's crawling babies from the foot: pods and shaft as a graphic block, the babies climbing at different heights, soft sky. Strong, odd, unmistakably Prague. Prior.

Straight down from the TV tower on Žižkov's orange roofs, the round park in the middle, St Ludmila's spires far left. Through glass: washed contrast and a haze over the far city, no reflections visible. Good subject, held back by the glass.

The Žižkov Jewish cemetery in colour: crowded stones under trees, a path and lawn across the bottom third, a rope line. A record; the colour adds nothing the twin in black and white doesn't do better. Prior.

frames.critique: A row of turreted facades going amber in the last sun, receding left into the light, clean sky. The best of the evening-gold facades: rich, ordered, the light is the subject. A lamp post at left. Prior.

A single stepped gable lit gold in the last sun, the relief figures readable, framed by black trees against a clean blue sky. Minimal and graphic; tighter and cleaner than 6506. Mihail at review: maybe better than 6506. A group loser to 6500 at the first look.

Riegrovy sady at sunset: a woman walking up the path, the sun bursting through the tree at right, St Vitus small on the skyline. Lovely light and a person in it, but a lamp post stands in dead centre and splits the frame. Blemish costs the star.

The National Museum's domes catching the last light, but the trees cover the middle, a concrete bridge runs across the bottom and a black office block crowds the right. The magistrála's clutter wins.

The west spires from below with a cloud bank at left and a stray roof corner bottom left. Good stone and sky; repeats 6585 less well.
The neo-Gothic Old Provost's house: brick, a gabled bay, a stone saint on the corner, blue sky. Sharp and neat; architecture as a record. Posted (slide 7).

frames.focus: sharp at 0.50,0.60 (copper roof and the tracery parapet)
frames.critique: St Vitus's chevet: the flying buttresses and pinnacles, green copper chapel roofs in a row, cloud breaking to blue. The Gothic machinery seen whole, well lit. Posted (slide 9).

frames.focus: sharp at 0.57,0.55 (the bronze group of the fountain)
frames.critique: Straight down from the tower on the third courtyard: the paving grid, people with long shadows, the round fountain sculpture and a wet streak trailing from it. Graphic and human, a view nobody else in the set has.

From the tower: the green rooster weathervane in the foreground, St George's red front and white towers, the roofs, the Vltava and its bridges running away. Layered and placed. The rooster's base cut at the bottom edge. Mihail at review: in.

frames.focus: sharp at 0.66,0.43 for the distance; the far city is softened by haze, not focus
frames.critique: Prague from the tower: Malá Strana's roofs, St Nicholas's dome, the river and Charles Bridge, the whole city to the horizon under a cloud deck. The establishing shot of the Castle day. Light is soft, not flat. Prior.

From the tower on the third courtyard and the palace wing, the town's roofs above: people scattered over the paving, the round sculpture at the bottom. Says more of the place than 6682 but is less of a picture; one of the two. Prior.

frames.focus: sharp at 0.62,0.40 (the chandelier); high-ISO grain in the vault
frames.critique: Vladislav Hall: the looping ribs of the vault, three chandeliers receding, the long plank floor, people small at the far end for scale. Warm light from the windows. The rope barriers along the sides are the only clutter. Posted (slide 9).

Looking straight up into Vladislav Hall's ribbed vault: the curves interweave, warm stone. A pattern picture; the top of a canopy at the bottom edge interrupts it. Pairs with 6704 rather than standing alone. Posted (slide 10).

The Castle steps at noon: St John Nepomuk's statue at left, the steps rising to the sgraffito tower, a woman climbing on the right, cloud breaking to blue. Full of the place, well balanced. The best of the three versions of the steps.

A vaulted passage in Malá Strana: hanging lamps, a parked motorbike, a man at a café table in the bright courtyard beyond. Moody and graphic, the light at the end works. The figure is small; it reads as an aside.

Kaférna's doorway: the painted sign, house numbers, the green door, through it the man at his table, the shadow cutting the cobbles. A neat frame-in-frame; the brown bin beside the door is the first thing you see. Prior.

A Malá Strana lane climbing under a sgraffito bridge-arch, the cobbles leading straight in, cloud above. Strong geometry, flat light; a car at the far end. A good lane, not as alive as 6568.
Wallenstein Garden's pond: the Hercules group on its island, the palace wing, St Nicholas's dome and tower behind, big clouds. Complete and pleasant; the green water takes the bottom half. Prior.

A small boy in a red cap crouching to a white peacock that's half-hidden under a wall of ivy, its tail sweeping out across the gravel. A moment, funny and tender, good colour. Seen from behind. One of the set's few small human stories. Mihail at review: the story carries it; not a 4, out.

Wallenstein's sala terrena behind the fountain, the bronze statues lining the avenue, visitors walking, St Vitus over the roof, cloud and blue. Layered from water to castle, the garden in one frame.
The bronze archer in the foreground drawing his bow, the parterre and the loggia behind, St Vitus over the roofs. A good idea; the statue's back is to us and the sky is a white sheet on the left.

Wallenstein's dripstone wall whole, blue and white hydrangeas along its foot, two visitors on the path for scale, a patch of blue. Shows what the wall is, where 6791 crops into it. Brought in from the reserve at review, in place of 6773.
Blue and white hydrangeas massed against Wallenstein's dripstone wall: soft petals against the grotesque, melting stone. Quiet, unusual, beautifully coloured. Prior.

A tall clipped hedge leading down a gravel path, St Thomas's spire and dome over the trees, two walkers at the end. Good leading line; the hedge is a large dark mass at left. Prior.

Loreta in the last sun: the bell tower and its green onion lit gold against a blue sky with thin cloud, the statues on the parapet in silhouette, a tree edge at right. Warm, clean, a proper cover. Posted cover.

Hradčany square in the evening: the Archbishop's palace lit at left, the Castle front and St Vitus's spires in sun, long shadows over the cobbles, a lamp at right. The upper half is empty sky; the castle sits small in the lower middle.
The Castle steps at 19:40: the same statue and sgraffito tower as 6733, now in cool shade with nobody climbing. Cleaner, emptier and flatter; the noon frame has the life.

frames.focus: crop landed on a plain stretch of facade: no shake, the cornice edge crisp
frames.critique: St Nicholas in Malá Strana from below in the last sun: the curved Baroque front gold against a deep teal sky, the green dome and clock tower at right, shadow climbing the base. Strong colour and form. Mihail at review: fine, but not a 4 and not an opener.

Mostecká to the Malá Strana bridge tower in late sun: the tower lit, the street full of people in shade, a 'pěší zóna' sign big at right. Lively and placed; the sign and crowd are a lot. Posted (slide 4).
A shaded lane to the Maltese church's tower, its red roof and the white cross on the banner lit. Clean geometry, people walking; most of the frame in shade, an umbrella at left. Posted (slide 5).
Čertovka from the bridge: the mill wheel at left, the water-sprite statue on its pole, the stream running to a pale terrace. A good subject in grey evening light; the wheel is a dark mass.

Charles Bridge's arches and the Old Town bridge tower and the Knights of the Cross dome in the last sun, from Kampa. Good light; the upper 55% is plain sky and the bridge is in shade. 6844 does it better.

The Old Town riverfront in evening sun: the bridge tower, the Smetana museum and the water tower, reflections running across the Vltava, the bridge's arches at left. Warm, ordered, a classic done well. A leaf intrudes at right. Prior.
(sheet only) rated 2 at the first look

A row of glowing yellow plastic penguins on a jetty rail at Kampa, the Vltava behind them and the Old Town bridge tower and Smetana museum lit in the evening. Funny, well lined up, the city still placed. One of the set's few light touches.
Kampa's houses in the low sun: ochre, mint and cream fronts, a café umbrella, cobbles with light patches. Pleasant colour; quiet, a little plain. Posted (slide 6).
An orange wall glowing in late light, four white windows, a pigeon on a lintel, a tree's shadow on the right. Minimal and warm, a nice breath in a sequence; small as a photo.
A Charles Bridge statue lit gold above the dark arch, a lamp, an orange wall at right and the far bank. Good light and shapes; two black umbrella shapes at the top left are puzzling.

A gable with a curved eyebrow over the window, a wrought-iron balcony with red geraniums and three lanterns, deep blue sky. Pretty detail, centred, nicely lit. Posted (slide 8). Mihail at review: a 4; minimal frames were undervalued.
The Old Town embankment from the bridge: the water tower, the gabled fronts gold, the weir and a small boat. Lovely light; repeats 6844 in a looser composition with a lot of sky.
(sheet only) rated 2 at the first look: a hand at the right edge

The Castle and St Vitus silhouetted against the sun going down behind the spires, Malá Strana's roofs and the riverside restaurants below. Soft, hazy, low contrast; the sun behind the cathedral is the idea and it works only gently.

The Knights of the Cross church: the green dome and pink drum lit by the low sun, Charles IV's bronze below in shade, pigeons on the ledges. Good colour, a solid architectural frame. Posted (slide 10).
The Castle skyline as a silhouette against the sun going down behind St Vitus, the river reflecting the glow. Wider and cleaner than 6862, a calm classic; dark and a little muddy in the town below.
(sheet only) rated 2 at the first look

A lane to St Gall's tower: the stone tower and its spire lit gold against blue, the street dark below. The tower is lovely; a 'Real Burger' sign hangs big at left and the crowd fills the bottom. Posted (slide 9).

The Old Town Hall tower in the last sun, the clock and stone glowing, deep teal sky, a slice of Týn's spires at the bottom right and the mural-lettered front at left. Clean, warm, strong. Posted (slide 3).

Týn above the crowd on Old Town Square in the last sun: the spires lit, the square packed with heads, cafés under the arcades. Says what the square is in July; the heads in the foreground cut in, the scaffold netting on the right tower. Posted (slide 2).
The astronomical clock in flat light: the dial, the apostles' windows, the figures, the bird-netting over all of it. A full record of the clock; no light, no angle beyond straight on.
Týn and the Marian column from the square, horizontal, the gables below in sun. Good light, but the left half is sky and the column; the church sits right. Prior; 6885 does it better.
(sheet only) rated 2 at the first look

frames.focus: sharp at 0.48,0.45 (the gilt Madonna on the gable)
frames.critique: Týn tight and vertical in the last sun: the spires and pinnacles burnt orange against teal, the gabled houses in front glowing. Rich colour and the shape fills the frame. Blue scaffold netting on the right tower is a blemish.

The Storch house on the square: the painted St Wenceslas on horseback, the oriel, stepped gable, all in warm last light. A lovely detail of the square, well framed; a record of a facade. Posted (slide 7).
(sheet only) rated 2 at the first look
Týn at dusk with the Marian column at left, the light off the spires, the gables pink. Cooler and calmer than 6885, the lit café below; less colour, less presence.

frames.focus: soft-intended at 0.20,0.60: the tram and the passenger are motion-blurred as meant. The passenger's profile is recognisable at 100% (assumed stranger). Arch edge not checked
frames.critique: A red tram sliding through a stone arch in Malá Strana, blurred with motion, its yellow-lit interior and a passenger at the window, the rusticated wall sharp around it. Movement against stillness; the most alive of the tram frames. Mihail at review: a failed photo. The concept is fine, the execution isn't: the blur has no shape. He'd have deleted it.

Charles Bridge at dusk from the Old Town end: the first lamps lit, a warm glow under the arch, statues and crowd in silhouette, the river, Malá Strana dark across, a lilac sky. Good mood; the top half is empty sky.
The Castle and St Vitus lit gold at blue hour above the dark roofs of Malá Strana, a pink sky, the riverside lights reflected. The classic view in the right light; a boat at left.

The Old Town embankment at blue hour from the bridge: the water tower and Smetana museum lit, the weir, the National Theatre's roof far right, gold reflections on the river. Rich and calm. Toss-up with 6915; this one has the warmer sky and the café crowd lit.
The same embankment a few minutes later: bluer, deeper, the reflections longer across the water. As good as 6908, a touch darker. One of the two.

ICM on Charles Bridge at blue hour: lamplight swinging into curves, the bridge tower and the Knights' dome ghosted, a figure in white. The light trails are pretty; the frame is a muddle at the bottom.

ICM, vertical: the bridge lamps pulled into bright wavy strokes, the tower and dome dissolving behind, deep blue. Simpler and more graphic than 6921; the best of the run. Intended blur; earns a place only as the one abstract frame in the river chapter. Prior.
(sheet only) rated 2 at the first look

From Charles Bridge after sunset: a lit lamp and a saint in silhouette at left, the Castle lit gold across the river, its lights running down the water, a clean gradient from deep blue to apricot. The best of the ten statue-and-castle frames: the lamp is lit and the sky graded.

frames.focus: sharp at 0.75,0.40 (the National Theatre's roof and statues)
frames.critique: The Old Town embankment in full night: the water tower, the lit fronts and the National Theatre's dome, long gold reflections over black water, a deep blue sky. The strongest of the three embankment frames (6908, 6915): richer and simpler. A purple-lit window at left.

Along Charles Bridge at night to the Malá Strana tower, lit warm, people in silhouette on the cobbles, a saint at right. Good atmosphere; a lot of dark sky and dark foreground, the tower scaffolded at left.
Mostecká at night to St Nicholas's dome and tower, lit white, walkers on the cobbles. Strong subject, but parking signs and a lit lamp take the left third and parked cars the right.

A Malá Strana street at night: the cobbles glowing orange under the lamps, a deep blue sky, a church front at the end. The orange-and-blue is lovely; parked cars, bins and a 'Blue Light' bar sign keep it a street record.
(sheet only) rated 2 at the first look
The arcades on Malostranské square at night: massive lit piers and lanterns, the empty road, a blue sky at the corner. Graphic and quiet; the road surface is a big dull area.

frames.focus: soft at 0.45,0.46: the destination sign shows a horizontal motion streak at 100%; reads sharp at display size
frames.critique: A red-and-cream T3 tram, number 22, swinging round the corner at Malostranské at night, its headlights on, the square's lit Baroque fronts and the dome behind, the rails curving away. The tram is sharp and the light warm. Better than 6959 on the site.
St Nicholas lit at night above the square's houses: the dome and bell tower gold against black. Strong lighting, but the top 40% is a black void and the street lamp flares.

From inside the Old Town Hall tower, through its open window: the painted gables of the square, the café umbrellas and the crowd below, the roofs running off. The frame-in-frame says 'up the tower' and the colours carry under the overcast. A crane on the skyline.
Týn through the tower's window, a stormy sky, the square's arcades below. The idea of 7129 again, but the bottom third is black window-sill and Týn alone through glass is less than the square.
The Old Town's roofs from the tower under heavy cloud: red tiles, a copper turret in the foreground, St Nicholas's green spire left, Pankrác's towers far off. Rich roofs, flat light. Prior.
